assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns a small molecule into a heterobifunctional or monovalent recruiter of an E3 ligase, so that proteins once considered undruggable can be removed rather than inhibited. It is a clear molecular design principle (induced proximity) that changed what chemists and clinicians can do, and it connects chemistry, cell biology and medicine.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept and its early peptide and then small-molecule realizations; Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work made PROTACs a general, drug-like platform. Handa, Ito and others uncovered cereblon as the thalidomide target, which makes the molecular-glue branch a separate discovery whose credit sits uneasily with the PROTAC trio.
assessment.maturity: Many degraders are now in clinical trials and the mechanism is confirmed across laboratories and companies. Approval of a degrader drug is still pending, but the chemical concept is already firmly established.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should combine PROTACs and cereblon-based molecular glues, which would change the laureate set.
I am recalling from memory the exact clinical status of degraders and have not verified it.
Credit between the Crews and Deshaies origin and the later medicinal-chemistry optimization is partly a matter of judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adding orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs and reassigned codons lets researchers install designed noncanonical amino acids into proteins in living cells, which is precise molecular design of biopolymers. It is original, widely used from biophysics to therapeutics, and a strong example of chemistry changing biology.
assessment.attribution: Schultz is the clear originator of site-specific incorporation in vivo and in eukaryotic systems. Chin made decisive contributions with orthogonal ribosomes, quadruplet codons and genome recoding. Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama contributed important enabling systems, but a two-person prize looks the cleanest.
assessment.maturity: The method has been reproduced and extended across many laboratories for roughly two decades, and the recoded-organism work shows continued development. The timing is more than adequate.
uncertainties: Whether Wang, Mehl or Yokoyama should displace Chin if the committee prefers an origin-only credit.
Genome recoding is still developing and may be better recognized later or separately.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The idea that condensates form by liquid-liquid phase separation reframes intracellular organization with physical chemistry. It matters for biomaterials, disease biology and the design of synthetic condensates, and many scientists now think in terms of it.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed P granules behave as liquids and set the framework. Rosen's multivalent-interaction work gave a quantitative chemical basis, while Pappu and Mittag developed sequence-grammar and physical principles. The set could readily be drawn differently, and there is no obvious unique trio.
assessment.maturity: Adoption is rapid and broad, yet debate continues on which condensates are truly phase-separated, how functional they are in vivo and on the limits of in vitro reconstitution. Part of the field is still maturing.
uncertainties: Biological function and physiological relevance are still argued in some systems.
Whether this is better placed with the Physiology or Medicine prize than with Chemistry.
The allocation of credit among five prominent contributors is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another at a target site without double-strand breaks, by fusing a deaminase to a programmable DNA-binding protein. This is a chemist's approach to genome editing, with clear therapeutic promise and high precision.
assessment.attribution: Liu's group made the decisive and best-characterized cytosine and adenine base editors. Komor and Gaudelli were the lead scientists on those papers, while Nishida and Kondo independently reported a deaminase-guided cytidine editor (Target-AID). If credit is to be limited, Liu is central and the other slot is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Clinical use is at an early stage, with first trials and patient treatments reported, which is a strong sign but not yet a long track record. The 2020 prize for CRISPR may shape how the committee sees timing and overlap.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 Chemistry Nobel for CRISPR-Cas9 and the choice between base editing and prime editing as the recognized advance.
Liu is the dominant name, so a second laureate may not be warranted.
My recollection of clinical trial progress is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminators and clonal clusters is a chemistry-driven advance that made genome sequencing cheap and routine, with massive effects on biology and medicine. Its impact is difficult to overstate.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman invented the Solexa chemistry and its single-molecule and cluster implementations. Others, such as Rothberg (pyrosequencing-based approach), Ju and Mayer, made separate contributions to alternative platforms, so credit across competing technologies is complicated.
assessment.maturity: The technology has been mature and ubiquitous for a long time, so recognition is not premature and may, if anything, be late.
uncertainties: Competing platforms make it unclear which contributions the committee would regard as decisive.
The prize may be viewed as sitting between Chemistry and Physiology or Medicine.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves noncovalent assemblies in the gas phase so that stoichiometry, subunit connectivity and ligand binding of intact protein complexes, including membrane proteins, can be read directly. It is a widely used analytical tool for biomolecular recognition, relevant to biosensing and drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Robinson drove the extension to large complexes and membrane proteins, Heck developed the methods and instrumentation for heterogeneous assemblies, and Chait contributed early protein MS and noncovalent-complex methods. Loo and Gross are also credited, so boundaries are fuzzy.
assessment.maturity: The approach is mature and independently validated in many laboratories, although it follows the 2002 prize for ESI and MALDI for biomolecules, so the committee may see it as an incremental advance on that.
uncertainties: Whether the committee considers it sufficiently distinct from the 2002 mass spectrometry prize.
The allocation among Robinson, Heck, Chait, Loo and Gross is not clear to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing of single molecules enabled direct, label-free electrical readout of nucleic acids and has become a portable sequencing platform. It combines protein engineering, chemistry and device design and has real translational impact.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Kasianowicz proposed and demonstrated the principle, Bayley engineered pores and chemistry for sensing, and Akeson showed processive enzyme-controlled reading. I believe Branton has died, which would exclude him, but I have not verified this.
assessment.maturity: Commercial sequencers exist and the method is validated, though accuracy and scope are still improving, and the conceptual attribution is argued.
uncertainties: Branton's status and whether a posthumous exclusion applies.
Uncertain who the committee would view as the primary inventor.
The technology is still improving, which could argue for waiting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programming nanoparticle assembly with DNA, and spherical nucleic acids as defined architectures, gives precise control over nanoscale structure, with colorimetric and plasmonic detection that I know well from biosensing. It has influenced diagnostics, materials and intracellular delivery.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin's group and Alivisatos's group published the foundational 1996 DNA-nanoparticle assembly papers close together, and Mirkin then developed spherical nucleic acids and detection schemes. Storhoff and Mucic were early coauthors, so a Mirkin-Alivisatos pair is the most defensible choice.
assessment.maturity: The concept is confirmed over nearly three decades and used commercially, though clinical impact of spherical nucleic acids is still modest, and Alivisatos may already be seen as covered by quantum-dot recognition in 2023.
uncertainties: Alivisatos overlapped with the 2023 Chemistry Nobel topic of nanocrystals, which may make a second prize awkward.
Clinical impact of spherical nucleic acids remains limited so far.
